title: KV prefetch economizer and weight fragmentation playbook
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a reproducible, low-risk approach to budget GPU resident memory across three competing pools: static weights, KV cache, and activation buffers, while enabling continuous batching without elevated OOM risk. This ticket proposes a two-part runtime change and a complementary simulation + observability stack: 1) a per-tenant Burst Credit Account (BCA) that accrues and spends "burst credits" to permit short-lived excess KV/activation usage, and 2) a fragmentation-aware weight residency policy that opportunistically offloads low-access weight fragments under pressure.

Background + motivation:
- Current behavior: static weight residency and eager KV prefetching cause unpredictable tail OOMs during microburst traffic even when average utilization looks safe. Continuous batching improves throughput but increases transient activation pressure.
- Goal: increase sustainable throughput (tokens/sec) and reduce OOM incidents by providing predictable headroom windows for mixed workloads while keeping latency SLOs acceptable.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Burst Credit Account (BCA) model:
   - Each tenant has an in-memory credit ledger (credits in MiB*ms equivalent). Credits accrue from long-term underutilization (credit generation rate) and are consumed by transient KV/activation overshoot.
   - Credits decay with a configurable half-life to avoid unbounded accumulation.
   - Admission control consults BCA: if request would exceed steady-state budget, it can be allowed if sufficient credits exist; otherwise it triggers soft-throttle (smaller batch, drop speculative prefetch) or fallback to a lower-capacity model variant.
2) Weight fragmentation + opportunistic offload:
   - During packing/placement we compute a per-weight-fragment LRU score based on recent kv-lookup/attention usage and size. Low-score fragments become eligible for ephemeral device->host offload when BCA is low.
   - Offload has hysteresis windows and prefer fragments with low access frequency to minimize perf regression.
3) Continuous-batch shaping heuristic:
   - Batch admissions are shaped using a per-GPU token buffer that accounts for pending tail activations. Continuous batching scheduler reduces batch headroom when BCA is low to protect activations.

Simulation and metrics plan:
- Built a simulator (serving/sim/kb-budget-sim v1) that models per-tenant request traces (chat-like mixes, seq-lens 16–4096).
- Early simulation results: ~12% median throughput increase on mixed workloads, 90% reduction in OOM events in the simulated tenant set with a conservative BCA config. Tail (95th) latency increased by ~3–8% depending on offload latency profile.
- Key metrics to ship with runtime: BCA balance (MiB-ms), prefetch hits, offload rate (fragments/sec), OOM/sec, continuous-batch drop rate, model-variant fallback count. Dashboards: https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/gpu-memory-budgeting (internal).

Implementation phases and artifacts:
- Phase 0 (research/sim) - DONE: simulator + traverse of config space. Notebook and sim runs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/sim-notebooks/bca-experiments.ipynb
- Phase 1 (runtime prototype) - IN PROGRESS: implement BCA ledger + admission hook in admission-controller and a lightweight fragment offload API. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4123 (WIP).
- Phase 2 (integration + canary) - NEXT: enable on a single Dedicated pool with synthetic load during low-traffic nights, wire metrics to console and add regression alerts (release: runtime-1.20).
- Phase 3 (rollout) - TBD: staged rollout with per-tenant tuning, automatic fallback policy.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Complexity vs. benefit: BCA adds cross-layer state and requires careful telemetry to avoid silent mis-accounting. We can mitigate by shipping as optional per-tenant feature (off by default).
- Offload cost: host <-> device transfer latency depends on hw and model size. For small fragments this is beneficial; for large fragments it can harm tail latency. We will constrain fragment size and use bounded offload concurrency.
- Quantized models and kernel selection: some kernels expect weights resident; ensure offload API integrates with kernel loader so we can block admissions until fragment is fetched.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2026-02-24: Ticket created. Initial hypothesis and sim config posted to confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Burst+Credit+Model.
- 2026-03-03: Ran 10k-scenario sim sweep across access-skew, seq-len mix; POC showed good headroom recovery. Notebook + raw data uploaded to Drive.
- 2026-03-05: Prototype offload API sketched; landed small shim in serving runtime to mark fragments as "evictable" (internal branch).
- 2026-03-10: PR 4123 opened to add BCA ledger and admission checks. Early unit tests green.
- 2026-03-12: Internal canary plan drafted; QA load script ready.

Review feedback and actions:
- Ava Patel (SRE): "Add a debug-mode that logs BCA ledger changes per-request but samples at 0.1% to limit noise." Action: added sampling flag in admission-controller (WIP).
- Noah Kim (ML Infra): "Quantize-aware offload: add a per-fragment metadata tag for quantization format so we avoid host-format mismatch." Action: will add fragment metadata and update kernel loader in Phase 1.
- Product feedback (Amelia Ortiz): "Customer-visible feature should default to opt-out; require explicit enable for Private deployments." Action: implement tenant config gate and opt-in flag in Console.

Testing and rollout criteria:
- Pre-merge: unit tests for ledger math, property tests for credit decay and accrual, and synthetic load tests in CI.
- Canary: reduce BCA config to conservative values; observe OOM/sec, fallback count, and latency SLOs for 48h.
- Success criteria: net reduction in OOM/sec by >=70% on canary tenants with <=10% regression in p95 latency and >=5% throughput improvement for mixed traces.

Blockers and risks:
- Blocker: need a merge from ENG-41207 (KV-prefetch telemetry refactor) to correlate credits with actual prefetch bytes; dependency tracked above.
- Risk: On heterogenous hw (NVLink vs PCIe), effeciveness of fragment offload varies; need per-region tuning knobs.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish PR 4123 unit tests and add sampled BCA debug logging (owner: Mateo).
- Coordinate with SRE (Ava) to schedule a single-pool canary (tentative 2026-03-24).
- Add quantization metadata to fragment descriptor and run microbenchmarks to measure offload latency threshold where offload is net-positive.
